'''Iseki Sanjinja''' (井関三神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto Shrine}} located in Nakagaitsu, within {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}{{ill|Tatsuno, Hyōgo|en|Tatsuno, Hyōgo|qid=Q877190|lt=Tatsuno City}} {{ill|Issai|ja|揖西村|ko|잇사이촌|qid=Q11498437|lt=Isai Town}}. It is designated as an {{ill|Old Hometown Shrine|ja|旧郷社}} and a {{ill|Former Sacred Offerings Shrine|ja|旧神饌幣帛料供進指定神社}}. The shrine enshrines the tutelary deities of the Hase clan, {{ill|Seoritsu-hime|ja|瀬織津姫|zh|瀨織津姬神|qid=Q13579836}}, and of the Wakisaka clan, {{ill|Takeminakata|ja|建御名方命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatemina no Mikoto|qid=Q9150391|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9150391}}, in a combined enshrinement.

== Enshrined Deities ==
=== Three Main Hall Deities ===
Three Great Deities of the Shrine  
* Iseki Daimyōjin – {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|天照国照彦火明櫛玉饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Kuniteruhiko Hikari Kushi Tama Hoyosui no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10949054}}<ref>{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|ja|播磨国風土記|ko|하리마 국 풍토기|simple|Harima-no-Kuni Fudoki|zh|播磨國風土記|qid=Q11498726|lt=Harima Fudoki}} states that he is considered to be the child of Oho Namuchi ({{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}}).</ref>  
: Bestows abundant harvests (via flood control and favorable weather), healing of illnesses (promoting health), national protection (soul pacification, land stabilization, and safety), enduring family fortunes (prosperity of descendants, safe childbirth, and harmonious unions), as well as benefits in aerospace, traffic safety, and iron production.

* Yase Daimyōjin – {{ill|Seoritsu-hime|ja|瀬織津姫|zh|瀨織津姬神|qid=Q13579836}}  
: Removes disasters (through purification, fortune enhancement, misfortune and evil luck expulsion, sin cleansing, and disease prevention), aids in river flood control (environmental conservation), and protects women (ensuring safe childbirth and child-rearing).

* Suwa Daimyōjin – {{ill|Takeminakata|ja|建御名方命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatemina no Mikoto|qid=Q9150391|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9150391}}  
: Patron of agriculture, hunting, sustained military success (victory), development (new settlement and industrial promotion), and national peace (prosperity, traffic safety, good fortune, and longevity).

=== Subordinate Shrine Outside the Main Grounds: Okumiya Shrine ===
* Okumiya Daimyōjin – {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeiwamitsuchi no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1502690|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1502690}}  
: Grants the fulfillment of heartfelt wishes, protection in martial endeavors (ensuring victory), safe travel, national safeguarding (through mountain management and environmental conservation), and disaster prevention.

=== Subordinate Shrines Within the Shrine Grounds ===
Ara Shrine  
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo no Mikoto}}  
: Patron of development, agriculture, and fire prevention (protection against fire disasters).

Inari Shrine  
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|en|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukano‐mitama}}  
: Bestows abundant harvests, prosperous commerce, and household safety.

Tenma Shrine  
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005|lt=Sugawara no Michizane}}  
: Confers academic success, encourages calligraphy and the arts, and offers protection from lightning.

Kotohira Shrine  
* {{ill|Ōmononushi|en|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}}、{{ill|Emperor Sutoku|en|Emperor Sutoku|qid=Q349287|lt=Sutoku‐in}}  
: Grants abundant harvests, traffic safety, protection from water disasters, household security, healing of ailments, severance of harmful ties, and exorcism of vengeful spirits.

== History ==
: According to the shrine legend, in the 2nd year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Sujin Tennō}}<ref>[http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6318017.html Hyōgo Prefectural Shrine Agency explanation]</ref> (which, as explained by sources such as the Hyōgo Prefectural Shrine Agency, is dated 96 BC by mechanically converting the imperial reigns recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} into the {{ill|Common Era|ar|الحقبة العامة|ary|إيرا عامة|as|সাধাৰণ যুগ|ast|Dómina común|av|НилӀер эра|az|Bizim era|be|Наша эра|be_x_old|Наша эра|bh|कॉमन एरा|bn|সাধারণ অব্দ|ca|Era comuna|ce|Вайн эра|cs|Náš letopočet|da|Vor tidsregning|de|N. u. Z.|el|Κοινή Χρονολογία (χρονολόγηση)|eo|Nia erao|es|Era común|eu|Oraingo Aroa|fa|دوران مشترک|fr|Ère commune|ga|Comh-Ré|gl|Era común|hi|आम युग|ht|Epòk nou an|hy|Մեր թվարկություն|ia|Era commun|id|Era Umum|ilo|Kadawyan a Panawen|inh|Вай зама|is|Okkar tímatal|it|Era volgare|ja|西暦|jbo|la cabna cedra|kk|Біздің заман|kn|ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಯುಗ|ko|공통 기원|ks|عام دور|kw|Oos Kemmyn|la|Aera vulgaris|lfn|Eda comun|lmo|Era comuna|lv|Mūsu ēra|min|Masehi|mk|Наша ера|ml|കോമൺ ഇറ|nl|Gangbare jaartelling|nn|Fvt.|no|Vår tidsregning|oc|Èra comuna|pa|ਆਮ ਯੁੱਗ|pl|Naszej ery|pt|Era Comum|ro|Era comună|ru|Наша эра|rue|Нашой еры|sh|Nova era|si|පොදු යුගය|simple|Common Era|sl|Naše štetje let|sr|Нова ера|sv|Vår tideräkning|ta|பொது ஊழி|te|సామాన్య శకం|th|สากลศักราช|tl|Karaniwang Panahon (kalendaryong Gregoryano)|tr|Milat|tt|Безнең эра|uk|Наша ера|ur|عام زمانہ|uz|Bizning era|vi|Công Nguyên|wuu|公元|yi|איצטיקע צייט-רעכענונג|yo|Common Era|zh|公元|zh_classical|公元|zh_min_nan|Se-le̍k|zh_yue|公元|qid=Q208141|lt=Common Era}} system), the deity {{ill|Amaterasu Kuniteruhiko Hikari Kushi Tama Hayasui no Mikoto|ja|天照国照彦火明櫛玉饒早日命|qid=DELETED_QID}} was enshrined at Kameyama in {{ill|Harima Province|en|Harima Province|qid=Q1047523|lt=Harima Province}}’s {{ill|Ibo District, Hyōgo|en|Ibo District, Hyōgo|qid=Q1042150|lt=Ibo District}}, and the shrine was established as Amaterasu Shrine.
: The shrine legend records:
{{quotation|
"In the 2nd year of Emperor Sujin, upon the raised platform there shone a brilliant light; in Harima Province too, a similar radiance was visible. In accordance with divine instruction, the Shidō Shōgun {{ill|Tanba-no-Michinushi-no-Mikoto|ja|丹波道主王|lt=Tanba Dōshun no Mikoto|lt_ja=丹波道主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Dōshun‐ō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 丹波道主命|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11368587}} of that time commanded, 'Establish a shrine within this sacred boundary,' and thus the shrine was founded."
|}}
<br />Furthermore, it is recounted that during a national pilgrimage, the deity {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeiwamitsuchi no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1502690|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1502690}}—enshrined as Okumiya Daimyōjin—expressed the wish, "Let my spirit abide here," and caused a large stone to be set up on the mountain peak. This miraculous event was duly reported by Shidō Shōgun {{ill|Tanba-no-Michinushi-no-Mikoto|ja|丹波道主王|lt=Tanba Dōshun no Mikoto|lt_ja=丹波道主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Dōshun‐ō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 丹波道主命|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11368587}}, and the stone thereafter served as the sacred body of the shrine.
: From that time onward, the deity {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeiwamitsuchi no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1502690|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1502690}}, enshrined as Okumiya Daimyōjin, came to be honored as Okumiya Taijin Shrine and was regarded as the guardian deity of the {{ill|ancient mountain fortress in Japan|ja|古代山城|zh|古代山城|qid=Q6431764}} and {{ill|Kinoyama Castle|ja|城山城 (播磨国)|qid=Q17211812|lt=Jōnoyama Castle}}. After the defeat of the {{ill|Wakoku|fr|Pays des Wa|it|Wakoku|ja|倭国|ko|왜국|my|ဝပြည်ထောင်|simple|Wakoku|zh|倭国|qid=Q10888424|lt=Wa Kingdom}} in the {{ill|Battle of Baekgang|en|Battle of Baekgang|qid=Q608727|lt=Battle of Hakusonoe}} during the 2nd year of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|en|Emperor Tenji|qid=Q314802|lt=Tenji Tennō}} (663 AD), a castle was built in anticipation of invasions from the {{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|qid=Q9683|lt=Tang Dynasty}} and {{ill|Silla|ar|مملكة شلا|ast|Silla (Corea)|az|Şila krallığı|azb|شیلا|bar|Silla|be|Сіла (дзяржава)|bg|Сила (държава)|bs|Kraljevstvo Sila|ca|Silla (Corea)|cdo|Sĭng-lò̤|ckb|شیللا|cs|Silla|da|Silla (koreansk stat)|de|Silla|eo|Silla|es|Silla (Corea)|eu|Silla (Korea)|fa|پادشاهی شیلا|fi|Silla|fr|Silla (Corée)|gl|Reino de Silla|hi|सिल्ला|hr|Kraljevstvo Sila|hu|Silla (ókori királyság)|id|Silla|it|Silla (Corea)|ja|新羅|ka|სილა|kk|Силла|km|ស៊ីលឡា|ko|신라|ks|سِللا سَلطَنَت|ku|Keyaniya Sillayê|lt|Šila (Korėja)|lv|Silla|mk|Сила (држава)|ml|സില്ല|mn|Шилла|ms|Silla|my|ရှီလာ|mzn|سیلا|nds|Silla|nl|Silla (Korea)|no|Silla|oc|Silla (reialme)|pl|Silla|pt|Silla (Coreia)|ro|Silla|ru|Силла|sco|Silla|sh|Sila (kraljevina)|si|සිල්ලා|simple|Silla|sk|Silla|sr|Сила (краљевство)|sv|Silla|sw|Silla|th|ชิลลา|tl|Silla|tr|Silla|uk|Сілла|vi|Tân La|wuu|新罗|zh|新罗|zh_classical|新羅|zh_min_nan|Sin-lô|zh_yue|新羅|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla}}, and the red Akamatsu clan ({{ill|Akamatsu clan|en|Akamatsu clan|qid=Q2659667|lt=Akamatsu Clan}}) held the deity in deep reverence.
: The timing and circumstances of the shrine’s relocation to Iseki—situated in the area of the present shrine, formerly the site of the original Okumiya near Kameyama—are the subject of various theories and remain uncertain. The present site of Iseki lies behind the oni‐gate of Jōyama Castle and is positioned diagonally opposite to the Jōzen‐ji Temple and the Miyauchi Tenmangū, which were established to ward off evil influences.

=== Chronology ===
* In the 2nd year of Emperor Sujin, at Kameyama in Ibo District, Harima Province (the present location of Okumiya), {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|天照国照彦火明櫛玉饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Kuniteruhiko Hikari Kushi Tama Hoyosui no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10949054}} was enshrined by imperial command, and Amaterasu Shrine was established; from that time, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武甕槌命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeiwamitsuchi no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1502690|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1502690}} was also enshrined.
* In the era of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|qid=Q335181|lt=Tenmu Tennō}}, the Shidō Shōgun enshrined {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Ushiro Tennō}}, which was later known in the late Asuka period as {{ill|Jingū-ji|en|Jingū-ji|qid=Q1074971|lt=Jingū‐ji}}.
* By the 2nd year of Enkyū (1336), during the turmoil of the Nanboku‐chō period, both the shrine and Jingū‐ji were destroyed by fire.
* In the 5th year of Jōwa (1349), the shrine buildings at Iseki were rebuilt.
* In the 12th year of Eikyō (1440), the Iseki shrine structures were reconstructed.
* In the 1st year of Kakyō (1441), both the Iseki and Okumiya shrine buildings were destroyed by fire during the Kajiki Rebellion, though they were subsequently restored.
* In the 1st year of Kōji (1555)<ref>The Nakagaitsu Chronicle records this as the 1st year of Tokuji (1306).</ref>, the headman of Nakagaitsu village from the Yase clan re-enshrined its tutelary deity, {{ill|Seoritsu-hime|ja|瀬織津姫|zh|瀨織津姬神|qid=Q13579836}}, by receiving a bunrei from the deity enshrined in Yase of Yamashiro City}}{{ill|Sakyō-ku, Kyoto|en|Sakyō-ku, Kyoto|qid=Q1321832|lt=Sakyō-ku}}: In present-day Yase, she is enshrined at the subsidiary shrine of Yase Tenmangū and Rokushosho Shrine.</ref>.
* In the 12th year of Kanbun (1672), when the lord of {{ill|Tatsuno Castle|ja|龍野城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatsuno Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10856352}}, {{ill|Wakisaka Yasumasa|ja|脇坂安政|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakisaka Yasumasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11612109}}, entered the domain, the guardian deity enshrined at Iida in Shinano Province—formerly worshipped at {{ill|Suwa Shrine|ja|諏訪神社}}—had its deity, {{ill|Takeminakata|ja|建御名方命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatemina no Mikoto|qid=Q9150391|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9150391}}, re-enshrined along with the three deities {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|天照国照彦火明櫛玉饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Kuniteruhiko Hikari Kushi Tama Hoyosui no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10949054}}, {{ill|Seoritsu-hime|ja|瀬織津姫|zh|瀨織津姬神|qid=Q13579836}}, and {{ill|Takeminakata|ja|建御名方命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tatemina no Mikoto|qid=Q9150391|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9150391}}, whereby the shrine came to be known as Iseki Sanjinja.
* Throughout the Edo period, the Tatsuno Domain lords, the Kyōgoku clan,<ref>After their reassignment to the Marugame Domain in Sanuki Province, the Wakisaka clan, Tatsuno retainers, and the villagers of Nakagaitsu and neighboring settlements contributed numerous offerings to the Iseki shrine.</ref> as well as successive generations of the Wakisaka clan, Tatsuno retainers, and the local chō (from Nakagaitsu, Shimizu, Shimizu Shin, Sae, Maechi) and Kuwahara Sō (from Oda, Shōbugai, Shingū, Kō, Tai, Takematsu, Kitayama, Ryūko) communities, held the shrine in deep veneration.
* In the 15th year of the Meiji era (1882), it was designated as a local shrine.
* In the 45th year of the Meiji era (1912), it was designated as a shrine for offering sacred foods and silk.

== Festivals ==
* 10‐Year Festival Revelation Ceremony  
A periodic festival held every 10 years, also known as the Revelation Ceremony. It preserves syncretic customs from the Shinto–Buddhist amalgamation period; at the time of the Jingū‐ji establishment during the Hakuhō period (circa 670 AD), the three revered Buddhist statues were unveiled.

* Harima's Extraordinary Festival: Sairen Bōzu  
Held annually on August 14 within the shrine grounds and on the following day at the grounds of {{ill|Ontoku‐ji|ja|恩徳寺 (たつの市)|qid=DELETED_QID|lt=Ontoku‐ji Temple}} in Nakagaitsu, this Bon festival commemorates the spirits of the Akamatsu clan who fell in battle during the Kajiki Rebellion at the fall of Jōyama Castle. It is designated as an {{ill|Intangible Cultural Property (Japan)|fr|Biens culturels immatériels du Japon|ja|無形文化財|tr|Somut Olmayan Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|qid=Q2901957|lt=Intangible Cultural Property}} of Tatsuno City.

== Legend of the Water Dispute ==
According to the shrine legend, 

{{quotation|
"In one summer when a severe drought gripped the land and all the people suffered from a lack of water, the villagers of Motokuni Koshibesō Shinohō (本國越部荘市野保村) ascended this mountain. They breached the embankment of the divine pond to divert water into Karaneko Valley and channel it into Shinohō Village. Yet, as the people dRank the water, both cattle and horses suddenly fell ill and collapsed.
Suspicious of this calamity, the villagers consulted an onmyōji. The diviner declared, 'This is divine retribution for having stolen and consumed the sacred water.'
Terrified, the villagers dammed the embankment as firmly as if binding a book, and conducted a grand purification ritual before the deities in hopes of atoning for their sin.
The residents of Hirai District in Kuwahara Village, witnessing the divine power that enabled the pond’s water to be restrained, came to venerate the deity thereafter known as Iseki Daimyōjin<ref>{{ill|Itatehyōzu Shrine|en|Itatehyōzu Shrine|qid=Q11458547|lt=Harima Provincial Shrine}}</ref>."
|}}
